title: Incident Evidence Workflow for Model Rollback and Data Sovereignty
author: Elena Park
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines a prescriptive, compliance-aware workflow for capturing, packaging, and retaining forensic evidence when a model rollback or emergency redeploy is triggered under cross-border data residency constraints. It integrates RBAC controls, audit-log collection, evidence manifesting, and chain-of-possession guidance so Security, SRE, and Legal can perform rapid triage and provide audit-ready artifacts for regulators or customers.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all Redwood-hosted inference incidents that: model rollback is required, or a model output led to customer-impacting data leakage, or a legal/regulatory request triggers an emergency rollback.
- Environments: hosted API (production), Dedicated (customer-committed pools), and Private deployments where Redwood controls audit collection.
- Not for pure development/testing incidents unless escalated to production.

Owners and Roles
----------------
- Incident Evidence Lead: Security on-call (primary), SRE on-call (secondary)
- Evidence Collector(s): SRE engineers with forensics training
- RBAC Approver: Identity & Access Management (IAM) lead or Security Manager
- Legal/Evidence Reviewer: Compliance counsel or CISO delegate
- Evidence Custodian: Secure evidence S3 bucket + immutability policy (see Packaging section)

Prerequisites
-------------
1. Access to audit-logging indexers (Elastic, BigQuery, or LogStream) and short-lived credentials for collectors (JIT activation).
2. Evidence manifest template stored in repo: infra/evidence/manifests
3. RBAC role names defined in the Auth catalog: roles/evidence-collector, roles/incident-viewer, roles/forensic-admin.
4. Preconfigured retention-profiles per region (eu-west-1, us-west-2, ap-southeast-1) in the Evidence Retention Registry.

Key Decisions
-------------
- We preserve raw request/response content only when incident impact assessment indicates legitimate need; otherwise we preserve metadata and reconstructed transcripts to reduce PII risk.
- Evidence bundles are immutable for the first 180 days and stored in the customer-region or legally-approved region for cross-border incidents.
- RBAC windows for collectors are timeboxed (default 4 hours) and logged to an entitlement audit stream.

Evidence Capture Workflow (high level)
-------------------------------------
1. Triage & Authorization
   - Incident commander invokes the Evidence Workflow Slack workflow: /evidence-start <incident-id> <region> <reason>.
   - Security on-call assigns Evidence Lead and files legal hold with Legal (if required).
2. Temporary Access Grant
   - IAM issues JIT credentials for roles/evidence-collector for collectors (max 4h).
   - Grant recorded to entitlement-audit topic with timestamp and justification.
3. Data Selection and Collection Plan
   - Evidence Lead completes the Evidence Manifest (see Appendix) specifying scope: model name/version, timeframe, customer tenant(s), regions, retention profile, and hash algorithm.
   - SRE runs selective collectors instead of full ingestion when PII risk is high.
4. Capture and Hashing
   - Collectors export logs, model KV cache snapshots, configuration snapshots, and request traces. Each artifact is hashed (SHA256) and recorded in the manifest.
5. Packaging and Sealing
   - Artifacts uploaded to the Evidence Custody bucket with server-side encryption (KMS) and object lock set to governance mode for 180 days.
6. Notification and Handoff
   - Evidence Lead notifies Legal, Product, and Customer Success and provides a signed manifest and access token for review.

Detailed Collection Matrix
--------------------------
| Artifact | Location | Collection Method | Min Retention | Notes |
|----------|----------|-------------------|---------------|-------|
| API request/response raw bodies | LogStream / GCS (region-specific) | subject to sampling and legal approval | 180d (if approved) | Prefer redacted copies unless legal requires raw |
| Token usage traces | Tracing system (Tempo) | Export trace IDs & full spans | 365d | Useful for latency/root-cause; avoid embedding PII |
| KV cache snapshot | Runtime profiling store (secure volume) | Runtime debug export | 90d | Contains model state; redact customer prompts unless approved |
| Model config + binary hash | Artifact repo + storage | git tag + checksum | permanent | Required for reproducibility |
| Authorization logs | Audit-stream | Query by principal & timewindow | 730d | Critical for RBAC evidence |

RBAC and Access Controls
------------------------
- Roles involved and minimum privileges:
  - roles/evidence-collector: read-only access to logs, runtime-debug-export, and push to evidence bucket. JIT activation only.
  - roles/incident-viewer: read-only access to manifests and summary artifacts. Assigned to Product/SRE leads.
  - roles/forensic-admin: can extend JIT windows and change retention on custody bucket (requires 2-person approval).
- All elevation events recorded to Entitlement Audit with fields: executor, approver, justification, start_ts, end_ts, reason-id.
- Prohibit use of permanent high-privilege keys for collection; collectors must use short-lived tokens.

Audit Logging and Collection Patterns
-----------------------------------
- Logging sources to snapshot: API gateway request logs, inference runtime logs, model routing decisions, configuration management events, and RBAC entitlement events.
- Use query templates (Evidence Query Kit) to ensure consistent capture windows and reduce noise. Example query (LogQL-like):

  {service=\"inference-gateway\", tenant=~\"^tenant-123|tenant-456$\"} | between(\"2029-02-19T12:00:00Z\",\"2029-02-19T13:00:00Z\")

- Exported logs must include UTC timestamps, request_id, principal_id, model_id, route, and sampling_flag. PII fields must be redacted unless manifest approves raw capture.

Data Residency and Retention Constraints
---------------------------------------
- Default policy: store evidence in the incident region. If region cannot host immutable evidence (policy/legal), use the approved cross-border escrow region list maintained by Legal.
- Retention tiers:
  - Regulatory incidents: retain 5 years or as required by jurisdiction.
  - Customer-impact incidents: default 2 years.
  - Operational incidents (no customer data): 90 days.
- For cross-border incidents: include export authorization code in manifest and record approval chain (Legal sign-off required).

Packaging, Hashing, and Manifesting
----------------------------------
- Each evidence bundle must contain an index.json manifest that lists artifacts, SHA256 hashes, collection time windows, collector identity, and legal approvals.
- Evidence bundle naming convention: evidence/<incident-id>/<region>/<bundle-ts>.tar.gz
- Example manifest fields (see Appendix).

Tooling and Example Commands
---------------------------
- Evidence CLI (internal): rw-evidence
  - Start a collection session: rw-evidence session start --incident INCIDENT-1234 --region eu-west-1 --justification \"model-rollback-suspected-leak\"
  - Run query export: rw-evidence export-logs --session SESSION-ID --query-file ./queries/tenant-1234-window.yaml --out ./artifacts/requests.jsonl
  - Seal bundle: rw-evidence seal --session SESSION-ID --artifacts ./artifacts --manifest ./artifacts/index.json --dest s3://evidence-custody/evidence/INCIDENT-1234/

- Collector checklist (one-liner):
  - verify JIT token validity, record token id in manifest, run export queries, compute SHA256 for each artifact (shasum -a 256 file), upload to custodian bucket, run rw-evidence seal.

Retention, Disposition and Legal Hold
-------------------------------------
- Default disposition is automatic after retention expires unless Legal places a hold. To place a hold, Legal must file a Hold ticket in the Evidence Tracker and set manifest.hold = true.
- Disposition requires two-person approval (Security Manager + Legal).

Post-incident Review and Evidence Audit
--------------------------------------
- Within 7 days: Evidence Lead delivers a summary to Incident Commander and Legal with a redacted artifact set suitable for public postmortem.
- Within 30 days: Evidence Audit by Security (sample-based) to validate that manifests, hashes, and custody logs match.
- Annually: Table-top exercise to validate cross-border packaging and JIT flows with participants: Security, SRE, Legal, Product, and a customer-privacy representative.

Appendix: example index.json manifest
------------------------------------
The manifest below is an example. Replace placeholders prior to sealing.

{
  \"incident_id\": \"INC-2029-00042\",
  \"region\": \"eu-west-1\",
  \"created_by\": \"elena.park@redwood.com\",
  \"collection_window\": \"2029-02-19T12:00:00Z/2029-02-19T13:00:00Z\",
  \"artifacts\": [
    { \"path\": \"requests.jsonl\", \"sha256\": \"<sha256-hex>\", \"size_bytes\": \"123456\" },
    { \"path\": \"kv-snapshot.tar\", \"sha256\": \"<sha256-hex>\", \"size_bytes\": \"987654\" }
  ],
  \"jits\": [
    { \"token_id\": \"tok-abc123\", \"principal\": \"sre.collector@redwood.com\", \"start_ts\": \"2029-02-19T13:05:00Z\", \"end_ts\": \"2029-02-19T17:05:00Z\" }
  ],
  \"approvals\": [
    { \"role\": \"legal\", \"signer\": \"priya.desai@redwood.com\", \"ts\": \"2029-02-19T14:00:00Z\" }
  ],
  \"retention_policy\": \"regulatory-5y\",
  \"immutable_until\": \"2029-08-19T00:00:00Z\"
}
